newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakh dealers see T-bill yields roughly unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Kazakh dealers see T-bill yields roughly unchanged.

text.p: Yields on Kazakh Treasury bills are likely to remain stable at the next few auctions due to a seasonal slackening of business activity and quarterly shortages of cash, dealers said on Monday.
"There is less money on the market, which means less active participation in auctions and lower demand," said Serik Zhukenov, chief dealer at ABN-AMRO Bank Kazakhstan.
Zhukenov said that to some extent this lack of money is caused by seasonal payments to the state budget.

"This is the end of the second quarter, and many foreign companies working in Kazakhstan sell dollars to buy (the national currency) tenge and make their regular payments to the government," he said. "So these tenge go to the budget."
"The market is sluggish -- major dealers are on holidays, and some banks will not take part in the next few auctions," said Bank TuranAlem's Nurlan Mukhametzhanov.
Zhilstroibank's Asan Buranbayev said demand had stabilised. "Yields have reached their 'golden mean'."
At an auction of 12-month discount MKM Treasury bills on Monday, bids for the paper averaged an annualised 16.69 percent, a securities expert at the Kazakhstan Stock Exchange told Reuters.

Quoting the National Bank's preliminary data, he said the yield at auction of 12-month paper edged down to 15.35 percent annual from 15.74 percent at the last auction on June 2, when the yield fell sharply from 22.59 percent annual.
Official data are due on Tuesday.
The finance ministry is offering 500 million tenge of three-month T-bills on Tuesday, and dealers say they do not see large changes of yields on this paper as well.
Yields on three-month paper eased to 12.84 percent at the previous auction on July 8 from 13.10 percent on July 1.
